title: SCONE: A Logic Locking Technique Utilizing SMT Solver and Circuit Encoding Scheme for Efficient Hardware IP Protection
problem: Stripped-Functionality Logic Locking (SFLL) with Distance-2 Protected Input Patterns (D2PIPs) provides security but faces scalability challenges, lacks flexibility in key derivation, and shows vulnerabilities to advanced structural attacks.
method: SCONE combines a Satisfiability Modulo Theories (SMT) solver with a novel secure circuit encoding scheme to generate protected input patterns. SMT enables scalable constraint satisfaction; the encoding scheme provides security against structural attacks while maintaining flexibility in key space design.

title: From Path-Aware to Application-Aware Source Routing using Traffic Classes
problem: Traffic engineering (TE) must make difficult decisions about capacity planning, flow allocation, and traffic splitting among paths to minimize congestion. Source routing enables fine-grained control but traditional approaches lack application-aware decision making.
method: Extends source routing (PolKA) with traffic classification at the network edge. Develops traffic class patterns and queuing methods for fair allocation across classes. Leverages in-band network telemetry (INT) and P4 programmability for classification and routing decisions.

title: WarmCache: Exploiting STT-RAM Cache for Low-Power Intermittent Systems
problem: Energy harvesting systems (EHS) suffer from compulsory cache misses after power failures because volatile SRAM caches lose all data across power outages, forcing cold-start cache rebuilding on each power restoration. Existing non-volatile cache designs impose high write energy and latency overhead.
method: WarmCache uses an STT-RAM cache with relaxed thermal stability (reduced retention time) tuned so cache contents survive typical power outage durations without requiring full non-volatile persistence. The compiler partitions the program into regions and performs region-level error correction: at each region boundary, updated cache lines are scrubbed and any multi-bit retention errors trigger re-execution of that region. A region formation technique via stitching (combining short regions) and splitting (dividing long regions) aligns region boundaries with the STT-RAM scrubbing interval.

title: A 28nm 0.22μJ/Token Memory-Compute-Intensity-Aware CNN-Transformer Accelerator with Hybrid-Attention-Based Layer-Fusion and Cascaded Pruning for Semantic-Segmentation
problem: Hybrid CNN-Transformer models (ConvFormers) for semantic segmentation suffer from large token-length demands (>16K TL), creating three challenges: (1) sparse attention cannot buffer attention feature-maps on-chip at high sparsity, (2) layer-fusion is infeasible due to simultaneous K/V/weight buffering constraints, (3) low sparsity in segmentation head limits zero-skipping effectiveness.
method: 28nm hybrid CNN-Transformer accelerator using memory-compute-intensity-aware dataflow, hybrid-attention-based layer-fusion avoiding redundant K/V and weight external-memory-access (EMA), and cascaded pruning targeting both backbone and segmentation head, achieving 0.22μJ/token.

title: Late Breaking Results: Warpage-Aware Generative Floorplanning for Reliable Advanced Packaging
problem: Advanced IC packaging introduces heterogeneous materials and dense interconnects, causing thermal warpage that degrades system performance and reliability during floorplanning optimization.
method: A transformer-based encoder learns node and edge representations from the floorplan graph. Parallel decoding combined with warpage-aware legalization jointly minimizes die displacement and warpage distortion, integrating thermal-mechanical coupling constraints into the optimization loop.

title: CrossBit: Bitwise Computing in NAND Flash Memory with Inter-Bitline Data Communication
problem: Existing in-flash processing (IFP) architectures can only perform bitwise operations on data sensed within the same bitline, preventing computation involving data from different bitlines. This restriction makes prior IFP designs unable to implement error correction codes (ECC) or efficiently process database query operations that require inter-bitline data interactions.
method: CrossBit extends commodity NAND flash memory with minimal additional circuitry to support both intra-bitline and inter-bitline bulk bitwise operations. It introduces inter-bitline communication pathways that allow data sensed from different bitlines to interact during in-flash compute. This enables in-flash ECC (IF-ECC) operations directly on MLC flash cells, which eliminates the prior restriction to SLC-only IFP. The same inter-bitline capability is leveraged to accelerate fundamental database selection and join queries that previously required data movement across bitlines.

title: 8.9 An On-Cell Monitoring and Balancing System with Near-Field Communications for EV Batteries
problem: Battery management systems (BMS) for EVs and grid storage require per-cell monitoring and charge balancing with reliable contactless communication and robust network formation, but traditional wired monitoring scales poorly with cell count (up to 216 cells).
method: On-cell distributed BMS architecture with per-cell monitor (CM) chips performing contactless serial communication to a system hub (SH); architecture includes per-cell processing, data storage, and charge balancing with network robustness through serial contactless protocol and dynamic network formation supporting up to 216 CMs per SH.

title: A UCIe Optical I/O Retimer Chiplet for AI Scale-up
problem: High-bandwidth AI accelerator interconnects require low-latency optical I/O solutions to scale multi-chip systems while maintaining signal integrity across chiplet boundaries.
method: Specialized chiplet implementing UCIe-compliant optical I/O retiming with integrated optical transducers and signal conditioning to bridge electrical and optical domains for chiplet communication.

title: 33.5 A 224GHz 19.9% TR Varactor-Less VCO Utilizing a Multi-Section Switch-Loaded Coupled-Line Resonator
problem: THz and sub-THz circuits require tunable elements like voltage-controlled oscillators (VCOs) and passive phase shifters, but varactors suffer from low Q-factor at frequencies >100GHz with limited tuning range, while switched-capacitor banks suffer from high OFF-state capacitance and low Q-factor.
method: 224GHz varactor-less VCO using multi-section switch-loaded coupled-line resonator achieving 19.9% tuning range through switched-inductor elements, overcoming varactor limitations and achieving high Q-factor at sub-THz frequencies.

title: AMRaCut: Scalable Partitioning for Adaptive Mesh Refinement
problem: Mesh partitioning for distributed PDE solvers faces trade-offs between partition quality and parallel scalability. Traditional methods (spatial ordering, multi-level graph partitioning) don't scale efficiently for AMR workloads with dynamic mesh evolution.
method: AMRaCut: Distributed-parallel mesh partitioner using parallel label propagation and graph diffusion. Operates mostly locally on initial partitions, limiting inter-process communication to neighboring processes. Leverages AMR's property of mostly local changes.

title: DM-Tune: Quantizing Diffusion Models with Mixture-of-Gaussian Guided Noise Tuning
problem: Diffusion models require high computational and memory resources; traditional full-precision execution is inefficient; naive mixed-precision quantization adds runtime overhead from format casting and management complexity.
method: DM-Tune replaces complex mixed-precision strategies with a unified low-precision format augmented by noise-tuning fine-tuning. Noise-tuning reconstructs mixed-precision outputs via a parameterized nonlinear function (Gaussian + linear components). Framework identifies sensitive layers, models quantization noise, and provides custom low-precision GPU kernels supporting efficient noise-tuning.

title: Invited paper: Enhancing Design Automation with Quantum Algorithms for Chip Design
problem: Cell placement optimization to minimize Half-Perimeter Wire Length is computationally expensive in classical approaches, limiting scalability for large designs; quantum and hybrid approaches may offer speedup.
method: A flexible quantum-hybrid placement optimization strategy minimizes HPWL through both custom Simulated Annealing and D-Wave Constrained Quadratic Model solvers, integrated with OpenROAD flow for layout and routing; validated on ASAP7 7nm PDK with real-world case studies.

title: Orchestrating Quantum-HPC Workflows with Distributed Quantum Circuit Cutting
problem: Quantum computers are limited by qubit counts, preventing execution of large-scale quantum algorithms
method: Qdislib: distributed quantum circuit cutting library with graph-based circuit representation, wire/gate cutting, support for Qiskit/Qibo

title: Compression Error Sensitivity Analysis for Different Experts in MoE Model Inference
problem: Serving large Mixture of Experts models under GPU memory constraints requires offloading non-activated experts. Expert offloading between GPU and main memory creates data transfer bottlenecks that must be addressed via compression.
method: Apply error-bounded lossy compression (SZ3, CuSZp) to non-activated experts. Analyze how compression errors in different network layers affect inference accuracy through extensive experiments.

title: SmartIO: A Lightweight End-to-End Workflow for Runtime I/O Optimization of HPC Systems
problem: I/O subsystem is a critical bottleneck in HPC systems. Existing optimization approaches require offline tuning, exhaustive parameter searches, or extensive ML model training - all time-consuming and resource-intensive.
method: SmartIO uses context-free grammars to predict future I/O calls during runtime, learns I/O characteristics from predictions, applies rules-based mapping engine constructed from literature review and empirical evaluation to optimize I/O operations proactively.

title: Late Breaking Results: Statistical Timing Graph Scheduling Algorithm for GPU Computation
problem: Statistical Static Timing Analysis (SSTA) handles on-chip variations by propagating timing distributions; computational complexity demands huge memory and runtime, limiting scalability to large designs.
method: Statistical timing graph (STG) scheduling algorithm for GPU execution; memory management strategy optimized for GPU memory constraints; tested on 18.2 GB STG workload.
